outbound_field_diff.py:196: `raw_baseline = (prev_snapshot or {}).get(jira_key)` — a prev-body read that yields {} under a key-set prev

findings.finding: The plan presents an exhaustive-sounding enumeration of prev-shape-sensitive consumers ('The prev-shape-sensitive consumers exercised here are check_dual_identity_complete and the differ's local-only/emit-both arms'), but a Read of the outbound field-diff path shows an additional prev_snapshot field-body consumer the enumeration omits: compute_update_fields reads `raw_baseline = (prev_snapshot or {}).get(jira_key)` (outbound_field_diff.py:196), and prev_snapshot is threaded into it in production (run_differs.py:523 → outbound_differ.py:746). Under a key-set prev this fallback collapses to `{}` (canonical_baseline=None). Production is safe ONLY because the code takes the `binding_store.get_baseline(local_id)` branch (outbound_field_diff.py:192-194, seeded by _advance_baselines at reconcile.py:576) — an unstated, empirically-checkable premise that binding_store+local_id are always present. The G1 corpus does not exercise this path (it only calls compute_mutations, keyset_prev_snapshot_corpus.py:64), so its 'zero difference' evidence does not cover it.
findings.location: Plan 'Shape constraint' paragraph; outbound_field_diff.py:196, outbound_differ.py:746, run_differs.py:523
scenarios: A production or test outbound-update path that reaches compute_update_fields without a binding_store baseline for a bound key (e.g. a cold-start binding whose baseline was not yet advanced) would fall to the prev_snapshot branch, get {} under key-set prev, and arbitrate against a null baseline — a different field-diff outcome than under full prev.
findings.suggested_fix: Add outbound_field_diff.py / outbound_differ.py to the Files/consumer list, state that the prev_snapshot arg there is only a fixture fallback and production uses binding_store baselines (seeded by _advance_baselines at reconcile.py:576), and either extend the corpus to assert the outbound field-diff produces identical results under full vs key-set prev for a bound key, or add a unit test asserting the binding_store-baseline branch is taken (so the prev fallback is unreachable in production).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite ADR 0026 in the safety rationale and state explicitly that narrowing prev_snapshot is safe only because the three-way-merge ancestor now lives in the per-binding baseline (binding_store.get_baseline, advanced each pass by A4-1), so the assignee-clobber regression (16870dbec / REB-532) cannot re-open.
evidence: Plan enumerates prev-shape-sensitive consumers as 'check_dual_identity_complete and the differ's local-only / emit-both arms' plus the binding walk — the direction-arbitration consumer is not named and ADR 0026 is never cited.

docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md Consequences: 'removing prev_snapshot without a replacement last-synced store re-opens 16870dbec and is explicitly rejected (the "corrected P4")' — the direct prior-art constraint on this migration.
ADR 0026 Context: prev_snapshot was the common ancestor for _local_matches_prev arbitration; regression 16870dbec / REB-532 was the live-verified assignee-clobber it prevents.

Codebase shows the precondition is met: outbound_fields.py:401-403 and outbound_field_diff.py:192-197 now source the ancestor from binding_store.get_baseline(local_id), with prev_snapshot fields only a fixture-path fallback; reconcile.py:_advance_baselines advances the per-binding baseline each pass (story d6bd).
The plan's stated dependency 'Depends on A4-1' is the likely installer of that per-binding baseline, but the plan does not connect the safety of narrowing to it.
findings.finding: The plan justifies the prev_snapshot narrowing migration empirically (corpus G1) but never references ADR 0026, the governing prior-art record establishing that prev_snapshot's field payload was the load-bearing three-way-merge baseline whose removal was explicitly rejected 'without a replacement last-synced store'. The migration is only safe because A4-1 moved that ancestor into per-binding baselines (get_baseline), and the plan should cite that prior art rather than leave the precondition implicit.
findings.location: Plan section 'Why this is safe — gate G1' and 'Shape constraint' consumer enumeration
scenarios: A reviewer or future implementer evaluating whether narrowing prev_snapshot could re-open the assignee-clobber regression (16870dbec / REB-532) finds no acknowledgement of ADR 0026 in the plan.

If A4-1 (the per-binding baseline) were reverted or its baseline advance regressed, the plan's stated safety argument would silently no longer hold, because it never made the dependency on that replacement store explicit.
findings.suggested_fix: In 'Why this is safe', add a sentence noting that prev_snapshot's historical role as the direction-arbitration ancestor (ADR 0026) has been superseded by the per-binding baseline installed in A4-1, and that the differ's outbound field-diff now reads binding_store.get_baseline(local_id) rather than prev_snapshot field bodies — making the field payload redundant for arbitration.
